newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-G.E. Crane says outlook still tough.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-G.E. Crane says outlook still tough.

text.p: Metal distribution and building products supplier G.E. Crane Ltd said on Monday the outlook for the company remains tough with the Australian housing industry unlikely to improve until late in the 1996/97 year.
However, the company said benefits stemming from recent acquisitions should help to improve its financial position.
"Although indications are that the housing cycle has bottomed, the going looks likely to remain tough," managing director John Ingram said in a statement.
"Any improvement in the Australian building industry during 1996/97 is expected to be modest and to occur late in the year."
In June, G.E. Crane bought the Melbourne-based Alumex extrusion business for between A$8 million and A$9 million.
The acquisition followed the company's purchase in November last year of plumbing supplies business Raymor Group for about A$33 million.
Earlier, the company reported an annual net profit of A$20.54 million, down from A$24.22 million in the previous year.
Ingram said he was pleased with the result in light of the difficult housing market conditions.

"1995/96 was always going to be a tough year due to the difficult market conditions presented by the housing cycle," he said. "This is a solid result given the circumstances and the net profit fell within our expected range."
The company declared a fully franked final dividend of 25 cents, in line with last year and making 45 cents for the year.
